h1: Black Tie Optional Wedding Guest Dresses: What the Code Actually Obliges You To
intro: Black tie optional wedding guest dresses run from a floor-length evening gown down to a dressy cocktail dress, and the Emily Post Institute also accepts a little black dress or dressy separates. What the code rules out is daywear: anything you would wear to the office or to a casual party. Length gives you room to choose; fabric is where most guests go wrong.
answer: For black tie optional, wear a floor-length evening gown, a dressy cocktail dress, a little black dress or dressy separates, which is the Emily Post Institute's list. A midi or knee-length dress is fine if the fabric is formal: satin, velvet, silk crepe, heavy georgette or sequins. Skip cotton, linen, jersey and anything that reads as daywear.

contentSections.heading: Black tie optional wedding guest dresses: what the code allows
contentSections.content:
The Emily Post Institute's attire guide gives women four options for black tie optional: a formal floor-length evening gown, a dressy cocktail dress, a little black dress, or dressy separates. Compare that with full black tie, which lists a floor-length gown, a dressy cocktail dress, or your dressiest little black dress. The difference is small. Optional adds dressy separates and relaxes the little black dress from your dressiest to simply a good one. The word optional is mostly about the men, for whom a dark suit becomes acceptable in place of a tuxedo.

So a midi or a knee-length dress is not a compromise here; it is on the list, as long as it is a dressy cocktail dress. The test is whether the dress would look at home at an evening party in a hotel ballroom. A matte cotton shift would not; the same cut in duchess satin would.

Read the start time too. Emily Post advises erring toward formality for semi-formal events after 6 p.m., and the same logic applies here: a six o'clock ceremony followed by dinner and dancing rewards a longer hem and a more formal fabric than a two o'clock ceremony with the same wording. At a daytime black tie optional wedding, a tea-length or midi dress with some sheen is right at home.

contentSections.heading: Choose a fabric that reads formal at night
contentSections.content:
Velvet absorbs light instead of reflecting it, so it looks rich under warm reception lighting and flat at a midday ceremony. Keep it for evening weddings from autumn through winter.

Silk crepe and heavy triple georgette are among the safest choices. They have enough weight to hang straight, they do not crease badly across the lap during a seated dinner, and they photograph as a clean block of color.

Duchess satin is beautiful and unforgiving. It throws a hard band of light along every curve, and a camera flash can blow that band out to white. If you love satin, a matte-face satin is easier to wear.

Chiffon needs a good lining. Unlined chiffon over a nude slip can turn semi-transparent under uplighting. Sequins are welcome at this code, provided they are stitched rather than glued and the base fabric is heavy enough to carry their weight without sagging off the shoulder.

contentSections.heading: Where should the hem fall?
contentSections.content:
Floor-length: aim for the hem to sit about half an inch off the floor in the shoes you will actually wear. A hem that pools gets stepped on by the third dance.

Midi: placement matters more than the label. The best point is the narrowest part of the calf, usually mid-calf or just below. A hem that stops at the widest part of the calf shortens the leg in photographs.

Tea-length, just above the ankle bone, is an underused option and an especially good one for a daytime version of this code.

Knee-length works when the dress is clearly a cocktail dress: a formal fabric, a defined shape, evening shoes. Above the knee is the length most likely to feel underdressed at an evening reception.

contentSections.heading: Check the construction, and the listing, before you commit
contentSections.content:
A formal dress shows its quality from a distance. Look at the lining first: it should run to the hem in something smooth, not stop at the hip. An exposed plastic zipper up the back of an otherwise formal dress is visible in every photo taken from behind. Boning that ripples through the fabric when you sit will ripple all evening. And be wary of anything sold as formal that weighs almost nothing; a gown that folds down to the size of a paperback will hang like a nightgown.

If the dress needs altering, allow time. Shortening a lined formal dress means shortening the lining separately, and taking in a boned bodice means opening it up. Book the tailor before you order, and work backward to your order date.

When you are buying online, the product page has to answer the questions a fitting room would. Before ordering, check:
- Fiber content. "Satin" on a listing can mean silk or polyester; both are fine, but a polyester satin under 100 percent synthetic lining can be warm through a long dinner. Look for the composition line, not the dress name.
- Length in inches, measured from the shoulder or the high point of the bodice, and the model's height. Compare both with your own measurement in the shoes you plan to wear; a "maxi" cut for a model of 5 foot 10 is a tea-length on someone of 5 foot 3.
- Whether the dress is lined, and to where. "Partially lined" usually means the bodice only.
- The closure. An invisible zipper reads more formal than an exposed one, and a long row of buttons needs someone to help you into it.
- The return window, counted against the wedding date. If you are ordering two sizes to try at home, both need to arrive, be tried in your real shoes and go back in time.

contentSections.heading: What 599 guest posts about this code ask
contentSections.content:
Black tie optional is one of the most-asked codes in our data. In our analysis of 10,700 posts on r/Weddingattireapproval (16 April – 21 October 2026), 599 mentioned black tie optional by name. Guests filed 369 of them under the subreddit's Black/White Tie flair and 138 under Formal, so most posters treat the code as a near relation of black tie rather than of cocktail.

What they ask is mostly whether something is dressy enough. Gown, floor-length or maxi appeared in 135 of those posts; cocktail dress in 36; midi in 30; jumpsuit in 16; tea-length in 8. The phrases "dressy enough" or "formal enough" appeared in 44 posts and "too casual" in 27, against 5 for overdressed. The worry runs one way: guests at this code are afraid of being under, not over.

The practical reading matches the Emily Post list. A floor-length dress ends the question, which is why most posters reach for one. A midi or knee-length cocktail dress is equally correct, but it is the choice that gets second-guessed, so it needs the fabric, the shoes and the jewelry to make the case on its own.

contentSections.heading: Adjust for the hour, the season and the venue
contentSections.content:
The words on the card stay the same from a June garden to a December ballroom; the right dress does not.

Daytime. A ceremony that starts before about four o'clock and ends with a late lunch is the easiest place for a midi or tea-length dress in silk crepe, a matte satin or a lined lace. Very high shine and heavy sequins look out of place in daylight.

Evening. After dark, length and sheen both move up. A floor-length dress, a velvet midi or a beaded cocktail dress all look at home. A plain knee-length dress can still work, but it now needs the evening shoes and jewelry to carry it.

Summer. Choose weight without heat: silk crepe, a lined chiffon gown or a structured cotton-silk blend in a formal cut. Velvet and heavy brocade are winter fabrics.

Winter. Velvet, heavier satin, long sleeves and a real evening coat. A coat is part of the outfit at a winter evening wedding, since it appears in every arrival photo.

Outdoor or garden venues. Black tie optional on a lawn or a vineyard terrace is still formal, but the ground changes the plan: a hem that clears the grass, a block heel or a dressy flat, and a wrap for after sunset.

Prints. Large, painterly florals and abstract prints on a dark ground hold their formality. Small, busy repeats such as ditsy florals, fine polka dots and thin stripes read casual from across a room and can shimmer on camera.

contentSections.heading: Dressing alongside a partner in a suit or a tuxedo
contentSections.content:
The optional in black tie optional is mostly about menswear. The Emily Post Institute's attire guide lists a tuxedo for men at this code, or a dark suit with a white dress shirt and a conservative tie. Partners came up often in our data: 78 of the 599 posts mentioned a husband, boyfriend, fiancé or partner, and 93 mentioned a suit, tux or tuxedo.

If you are attending as a couple, decide together so the two outfits sit at the same level. A tuxedo next to a knee-length day dress looks mismatched; so does a beaded gown next to a mid-gray suit. A simple rule works:
- Tuxedo: a floor-length gown or a very dressy cocktail dress in an evening fabric.
- Dark suit, white shirt, conservative tie: any dress on the list, including a midi or a polished little black dress.

The dark suit should be navy, charcoal or black, never a light summer suit, and the shoes should be polished leather. If you are both unsure, ask the couple which way most guests are leaning. A wedding party in tuxedos is a hint that a floor-length dress will be the common choice.

faqs.question: Can I wear black to a black tie optional wedding?
faqs.answer: Yes. The little black dress is on Emily Post's list for this code. Head-to-toe flat black can photograph as a silhouette with no detail, so break it up with a textured fabric such as velvet or lace, a metallic shoe or a strong earring.

faqs.question: Is a midi dress okay for black tie optional?
faqs.answer: Yes. A dressy cocktail dress is on Emily Post's list for this code, and a midi in an evening fabric such as satin, velvet, silk crepe or beaded lace qualifies. Place the hem at the narrowest part of the calf, wear a formal heel or dressy flat, and keep cotton, linen and jersey for other events.

faqs.question: Does a jumpsuit count?
faqs.answer: Yes, as dressy separates or an evening alternative, if the tailoring is serious: a crepe or satin jumpsuit with a proper waist seam and a lined bodice. A soft jersey jumpsuit reads as loungewear under bright light.

faqs.question: What shoes work for black tie optional?
faqs.answer: A closed or nearly closed toe in satin, suede or metallic leather. Check the ground first: grass, gravel, cobbles or an old terrace will swallow a stiletto. A block heel of two to three inches looks just as formal and lasts the night.

faqs.question: Which colors should I avoid?
faqs.answer: White, ivory, cream, the palest champagne, and anything that photographs as white under a flash, such as very pale blush, oyster and the palest silver. Beyond that, avoid matching the bridal party if you know its colors.
